sentences: Bare to the waist, wearing an amber necklace and a white cloth at her hips, a woman turns slightly and watches us with a searching, questioning look.
The German painter Paula Modersohn-Becker painted this self-portrait in Paris on 25 May 1906.
That February she had left her husband and the artists' colony of Worpswede to devote herself entirely to painting in Paris.
Although she appears to be pregnant, she was not when she painted it.
She is recognised as the first known woman painter to paint nude self-portraits, and as far as is known these pictures were not shown to outsiders in her lifetime.
The 'sixth wedding day' of the German title counts the wedding itself as day one, so the picture actually marks exactly five years since her marriage in 1901.
The following November, shortly after giving birth to a daughter, she died at thirty-one, and in 1927 her museum opened in Bremen as the first museum devoted to a single woman artist.
